target: whole: culm sheath (the blade is the culm-sheath blade, a sheath leaf's lamina), not the foliage leaf blade
fix: In bamboo descriptions (FOC Bambusoideae) 'blade' following the culm-sheath clauses (auricles, oral setae, ligule; 'erect, horizontal or reflexed') is the culm-sheath blade; the foliage leaves come after 'Leaves 2 or 3 per ultimate branch'. Carry the culm sheath as the whole slot.
reason: The sentence sits inside the culm sheath description (sheath colour, ligule, 'blade erect ... reflexed in lower culm, ... same colors as those of sheath'). Foliage leaf blades of Phyllostachys are lanceolate, not triangular, so the annotation is false for the foliage leaf without the sheath context. Values triangular / lanceolate-triangular are fine.
'Inflorescences erect, ± congested': congested inflorescence with an 'approximately' qualifier for ±.

fix: 'gaine foliaire ..., non ciliée sur le bord': the subject is the leaf sheath ('gaine foliaire'), and 'sur le bord' is its margin. The French head noun 'gaine' must not be dropped back to 'feuille'.
reason: The quality is said of the leaf sheath margin, not the whole leaf. The negation is right.
'stems subquadrangular' = stem approximately quadrangular.

fix: In Berberis (and Mahonia, here Berberis sect. Mahonia) the 'spines' are leaf spines: modified leaves at the nodes. 'Thorn' (a modified shoot) is the wrong class. Map 'spine' by taxon or context, not always to thorn.
reason: The absence is right, but the absent part is a leaf spine, not a thorn.

fix: A bare 'glaucous' describes a surface covered with a whitish waxy bloom (PATO glaucous). It should not go through the colour synonym table to 'green'. Only compounds like 'glaucous green' are colours. The 'approximately' qualifier is also spurious; nothing in 'glaucous.' gives it.
reason: 'Leaf-blades ... glaucous' gives the bloom, not the hue green.
Leaf apex obtuse (to subrounded): the lamina tip is substituted correctly and obtuse is the first value of the range.
'sparsely pubescent adaxially, more densely so abaxially': the abaxial surface is pubescent. The comparative density is lost, but the statement holds.
'Leaves ... to 2 mm': leaf length up to 2 mm, open lower bound.
Stem internodes 'yellow, pale brown ... when dry': pale brown of the stem with the dried condition carried. The mapping to light grayish brown is acceptable for ISCC-NBS 'pale brown'.

fix: In 'A and B or C' the 'and' binds tighter than 'or': the first alternative is the conjunction triangular + laciniate. Do not drop the first conjunct.
reason: Triangular (PATO_0001875) is missing. The lobes are either triangular-and-laciniate or linear.
Valves glabrous or (rarely) puberulent. Fruit valve (PO_0000033) would be more specific for a Draba silicle, but the generic valve (PO_0025228) is not wrong.

fix: A trailing position phrase 'at the apex' after a list of shape values ('obtuse, slightly emarginate or acutish at the apex') scopes the whole list to the apex. Substitute the bearer as is done for 'apex obtuse'.
reason: The flora says these shapes of the leaf apex, not of the blade as a whole. The alternatives emarginate (slightly) / acutish are right.
Vitex negundo leaves are palmately compound; '7–12 secondary veins' per leaflet, container leaflet. The count is right.
'Pétales 5' = 5 petals.
'floral bracts ... shorter than ovary': bract decreased length relative to the ovary.

target: higher order inflorescence axis / inflorescence branch (PO_0009081)
fix: 'branches spreading' inside an inflorescence description has 'branches' as its own subject: inflorescence branch, not the inflorescence (or the immature inflorescence before it).
reason: The spreading quality is said of the inflorescence branches.
'Capsule ... 3-valved' = 3 fruit valves.
Spikelets 2–3 mm long.
Upper glume subequaling the spikelet: length ratio about 1. An 'approximately' qualifier for 'sub-' would be better, but the reading holds.
Marginal teeth 50–100 per side of the blade.
'sépales de 5-10 mm de long' = sepal length 5–10 mm.

target: relation target: apex of the narrow part of the receptacle-tube (hypanthium / floral tube), not a bare 'plant organ apex'
fix: In 'inserted at apex of X', the target is the apex of X. Keep the 'of'-complement as the whole of the apex. Otherwise the relation points to no part.
reason: The insertion into the tube is right, but 'apex' alone loses which structure it is the apex of.
Figs (syconia, treated as fruit) depressed globose = oblate.
'fertile stamens 9': 9 stamens. Staminodes are given separately ('rudimentary').
'Capsule ovoid-lanceolate': a shape between ovoid and lanceolate, a continuum.

fix: 'bien visibles dessous' limits visibility to the lower surface. Carry the place slot (abaxial) when 'dessus'/'dessous' follows a quality.
reason: The secondary (additional) veins are conspicuous beneath. Without the side the statement may be false for the upper surface; it cannot be told from the text.

target: vascular bundle (PO_0005020), intramarginal vein; container leaf lamina
fix: In 'intramarginal vein indistinct' the subject noun is the vein. The modifier 'intramarginal' must not let the bearer fall back to the leaf.
reason: The vein is indistinct, not the leaf.
'étamines 10' = 10 stamens.

fix: 'nervures basilaires N' counts only the basal veins. Keep 'basilaires' as a position slot, otherwise the count reads as the total number of veins.
reason: 4–6 is the number of basal nerves of the leaflet, not of all its veins.
